Exercise: Cable Hammer Curls - Rope Attachment

Category:
strength

Exercise Type:
isolation

Force Type:
pull

Difficulty Level:
beginner

Movement Patterns:

- elbow_flexion
- bilateral
- supinated_grip

Primary Muscles:

- biceps

Secondary Muscles:
None

Equipment:

- cable

Fatigue Score:
3

Systemic Fatigue:
low

Stimulus To Fatigue Ratio:
2.5

Energy Requirement:
moderate

Recovery Time:
1 hours

Goals:
None

Contraindications:

- condition: Recent bicep injury, reason: May exacerbate existing injuries
- condition: Shoulder instability, reason: Can increase shoulder strain

Exercise Variations:

- name: Concentration Cable Hammer Curls, instructions: ['Attach a rope attachment to a low pulley and sit on the bench with your legs crossed.', 'Grasp the rope with a neutral (palms-in) grip and rest your elbow against the inside of your thigh for support.', 'Using your biceps, pull your arm up as you exhale until your bicep touches your forearm. Tip: Remember to keep the elbow stationary.']

Substitution Options:

- exercise_name: Barbell Hammer Curls, equipment: barbell
- exercise_name: Dumbbell Hammer Curls, equipment: dumbbells

Instructions:

- Attach a rope attachment to a low pulley and stand facing the machine about 12 inches away from it.
- Grasp the rope with a neutral (palms-in) grip and stand straight up keeping the natural arch of the back and your torso stationary.
- Put your elbows in by your side and keep them there stationary during the entire movement. Tip: Only the forearms should move; not your upper arms. This will be your starting position.
- Using your biceps, pull your arms up as you exhale until your biceps touch your forearms. Tip: Remember to keep the elbows in and your upper arms stationary.
- After a 1 second contraction where you squeeze your biceps, slowly start to bring the weight back to the original position.
- Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
